findings.statement: Partly fixed, still open. The new paragraph reads as a complete list of the design §9 agent choices that the design approval endorses, but it names only six. ADR-0006 restates at least four more §9 agent choices, and those still sit unmarked under owner-decision headings: (a) §9 bullet 7, the 'N exclue(s)' counter limited to explicit refusals, appears in D9 at lines 121-122 ('counts only the destinations the matched rules explicitly deny'); (b) §9 bullet 2, authenticated link delivery of media, appears in D6 at lines 81-83; (c) §9 bullet 6, a revision becomes a comment, appears in 'Fan-out and idempotency' at line 192; (d) §9 bullet 11, the new destination-disclosure-leak predicate rather than a new meaning for public-data-leak, appears at lines 233-236 and 257. The ADR-0005 amendment says its origin is 'owner decisions D8 and D10', but it also carries §9 bullet 5 (the popup delegates preparation to the editor, chunked delivery, the service worker holds nothing) without marking it. The list also names 'the refusal of non-conforming instances', which no part of the ADR body records.

findings.statement: This predates the bd822bd fixes; pass 1 missed it. The ADR header attributes the supersession of design §5.5 to '2026-10-24 owner decisions ... recorded in roadmap §4.2, §4.5 and §6'. The only §5.5 change is the rule that an unreadable visibility withholds the destination (reason visibility-unknown). Roadmap §4.2 records that rule in its 'Visibilité illisible' bullet, which is not labelled as an owner decision. In §4.2 only the rule precedence carries 'décision propriétaire du 2026-10-24'. The same change rewrote the design (§5.5 and §9 bullet 1), and that rewrite replaced an agent choice endorsed by the design approval ('lecture en échec traitée comme publique'). Severity is minor because the change is stricter, matches the approved §7 test ('une lecture de visibilité en échec fait retenir'), and comes from a roadmap the owner merged (signalement PR #23, merged 2026-10-24T06:23:08Z by constantin-jais). Still, Q5 asks for corrections that apply recorded owner decisions only, and the ADR presents a roadmap clarification as an owner decision.
findings.evidence: Carried forward unchanged from pass 2. ADR-0006:9-10 at HEAD is byte-identical to pass 2 (same file hash), and 3af298a cites no 2026-10-24 decision. Original evidence: ADR-0006:9-10 'they supersede design §5.2 point 5, §5.5 and §5.6 where they differ'. roadmap:211 labels only the 'Précédence des règles (décision propriétaire du 2026-10-24)'. roadmap:214-216 has no owner label. Fix: in the ADR header, name the visibility rule as a roadmap §4.2 clarification that aligns §5.5 with the approved §7 test, not as an owner decision, or have the owner label it.

findings.statement: New in 3af298a. The second clause of the v1-projection-only reopen trigger, 'or a v1.0 release candidate with fewer than four profiles qualified', makes a shortfall in qualification a reason to reopen the scope decision. The recorded consequence of that shortfall is the opposite: v1.0 does not ship. A release candidate with fewer than four qualified profiles violates D13. It is not a recorded reason to revisit D13. The first clause, 'an owner change to the v1.0 exit', already covers the legitimate route. The other four new entries have reopen triggers that need an owner decision or a new proposal.
findings.evidence: Design §3 'Comptes de qualification': 'Sans compte, le profil reste `unresolved` et la v1.0 ne sort pas (D13).' Design §2 B3: 'La v1.0 ne sort que lorsque les quatre sont `qualified`'. ADR-0006 D13 (line 158): 'The v1.0 exit is projection only, with four profiles `qualified` against real instances'. Fix: drop the second clause, or reword it so that a shortfall blocks the release ('… blocks the v1.0 release; it does not reopen this entry').

findings.statement: New in 3af298a. The v1-projection-only statement lists the four exact profile ids (github-issues/github.com/rest-2022-11-28, gitlab-issues/gitlab.com/rest-v4, jira-cloud/cloud/rest-v3, plane/self-hosted/rest-v1). Its anchor points to the D13 section, which names only the four families and instances ('GitHub Issues (github.com), GitLab Issues (gitlab.com), Jira Cloud, and self-hosted Plane'). The ids are recorded elsewhere in the same file, in 'Contracts' (ADR-0006:227-229), and in design §5.6 and the provider matrix. The entry claims nothing false. It is not the precision the brief asks for, because the anchored section does not hold everything the statement says. The anchor itself resolves.
findings.evidence: ADR-0006:156-163 (D13) contains no profile id. Running `grep -n 'github-issues/' docs/adr/0006-…md` matches only line 227 ('The exact profile ids of v1.0 are …', under '## Contracts'). The ids in the statement match provider-matrix.yaml and ADR-0006:227-229 exactly. Fix: either remove the ids from the statement (the families alone match D13), or accept the file-level source and note that the ids come from ADR-0006 'Contracts'.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Resolved through the PR #25 description. The description states the neutralization run and both gate-integrity answers for the test 'no v1.0 provider row is verified before its qualification'. Answer (2) depends on a `qualified` status that the current validator does not accept (ALLOWED_STATUSES = verified, assumed, rejected, unresolved, tools/ci/qualification.ts:13). The roadmap records this as planned: lines 402-403 say L5 extends the schema with `qualified` and a `profile` field. The answer is therefore consistent with the recorded plan.
resolvedFindings.evidence: `gh pr view 25 -R libre-ai/signalement --json body --jq .body`: 'the `plane` row set to `verified` in `provider-matrix.yaml` gives `Expected: not "verified"` … 2 pass / 1 fail; restored, `cmp` identical, 3 pass. Gate-integrity answers: (1) what turns it red is a v1.0 provider row set to `verified` before its qualification; (2) an equivalent refactor of the matrix does not turn it red, and neither does a legitimate later state, because L5 promotes rows to `qualified`, never to `verified`.' Roadmap:402-403: 'L5 l'étend au statut `qualified` et à un champ `profile`'.

limitations: Q(a): pass, except for F10 and F11. Each entry was checked against its source. v1-projection-only matches ADR-0006 D13: projection only, four profiles qualified against real instances, reproduction and verdict and the Customer Edge Bridge in v1.1, card under usable-verifiable, public page says so. v1-buyer matches D4 word for word. linear-target matches design §2 'Autres non-buts' ('Linear. Écarté au profit de Plane auto-hébergé (décision D3)'). standalone-cli matches D11: client, offline verification. 'Never projects on its own' follows design B6 ('Elle ne projette jamais seule'). It is weaker than D11's 'It never projects and never signs' but does not overclaim. multi-organization-operator matches D12 and design §2 ('instance hébergée servant plusieurs clients'). Statuses: two `verified` (decision recorded, as for the existing journey and canonical-record entries) and three `rejected`, worded as negations like the existing security-reporting and ai-authority entries. None claims that a capability exists.

Q(a) anchors: all five resolve to an existing heading by the GitHub slug rule. d13--v10-ships-projection-only-with-four-qualified-profiles (ADR-0006:156), d4--the-buyer-is-the-team-that-sets-the-rules (:50), d11--the-cli-is-a-client-and-an-offline-verifier (:136), d12--one-deployment-per-customer-one-organization-per-deployment (:142), autres-non-buts (design:82). No slug mismatch. `bun run check:qualification` checks only the path before '#' (tools/ci/qualification.ts sourcePath), so no anchor is machine-checked. The slugs were derived by a shell approximation of the GitHub rule and were not checked against rendered GitHub pages.

Q(b): pass. The three rejected entries match ADR-0006 'Alternatives rejected' (lines 245-249: Linear/D3, standalone CLI/D11, multi-organization operator/D12) one for one. standalone-cli and multi-organization-operator agree with decision-lock rows control-plane-cli-client and single-organization-deployment. The profile ids in v1-projection-only match provider-matrix.yaml and ADR-0006:227-229 exactly. project.v1.yaml situation ('la fiche restera sous usable-verifiable à sa sortie') agrees with v1-projection-only. Observation, not a finding: provider-matrix.yaml keeps a pre-existing `linear` row as `unresolved`. That status records no qualification and says nothing about targeting. It does not contradict 'not a v1.0 target', and none of the 21 non-v1.0 catalog rows carries a v1.0 marker either.

Q(c): pass. No dated Owner-arbitration marker in the diff or in the commit messages (both greps exit 1). The only added mention in scope is the prose 'n'écrit jamais de ligne `Owner-arbitration:`'. The four v1.0 provider rows are `unresolved`, and each opens with its exact profile id (provider-matrix.yaml lines 4, 6, 8, 24). 'status: accepted' appears 3 times in project.v1.yaml at 950135d and 3 times at HEAD. The nine added `status: verified` lines are seven pre-existing decision-lock and assumption rows reviewed in passes 1 and 2, plus the two new product-scope entries.
Q(d): F5 and F8 are carried forward unchanged. The files they concern have hashes identical to pass 2, and 3af298a does not touch them. F9 is resolved by the PR description.

Repeated observation from pass 2, not a finding: the two new `verified` entries cite ADR-0006, which calls itself 'proposed' until the owner's merge. They take effect in the same merge, following the ADR-0055 precedent.

This review is not owner consent or owner arbitration. It qualifies no provider, browser or deployment. I did not read the implementers' reports.
